# Numerical methods {.unnumbered #numerical-methods}

## Steady population solve {#steady-population-solve}

Linear rate equations are solved subject to population normalization. Self and unlike-alkali spin exchange depend on the electron marginal of the current population, so the complete steady state uses a fixed-point iteration and reports convergence and residual diagnostics.

Probability-conserving generators and collision maps are tested for normalization. Small negative numerical populations are not silently accepted as physical states.

## Spectral profiles {#spectral-profile-method}

Absorption and light shifts are evaluated from the real and imaginary parts of a shared complex Voigt response. This avoids switching to a far-wing (Delta/\Gamma) approximation near the Doppler-broadened line.

## RF resolvent {#numerical-rf-resolvent}

For a generator (G), source (mathbf s), and readout (mathbf r), the response is

$$
\chi_+(\omega)=\mathbf r^T(-i\omega I-G)^{-1}\mathbf s.
$$

The implementation diagonalizes (G=V\Lambda V^{-1}) once and evaluates

$$
\chi_+(\omega)=
\sum_k\frac{(\mathbf r^TV)_k(V^{-1}\mathbf s)_k}
{-i\omega-\lambda_k}
$$

over the requested frequency grid.

## Uniform optical closure {#numerical-optical-closure}

At every RF frequency, the physical-pump calculation solves a complex (4\times4) system:

$$
\left(I-\frac12PK\right)\bar{\mathbf u}
=\frac12P\mathbf b.
$$

The ordinary solver is used first. A least-squares solution is used only if the matrix is numerically singular. The maximum spectral radius of (PK/2) is retained as a feedback-strength diagnostic.

## Numerical invariants {#numerical-invariants}

The implementation explicitly protects:

- population normalization;
- trace preservation of density-matrix sources;
- Hermiticity of physical source and readout operators;
- consistent Hz and rad/s conversion;
- matched array lengths for plotted and exported frequency samples.
